questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Lebanon?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History & Data” part of the Lebanon article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Lebanon?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Lebanon on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Lebanon article.

questions.proof: It has borders with Israel to the south and Syria to the east and north.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Lebanon?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “The people of Lebanon” part of the Lebanon article.

questions.proof: The official language of Lebanon is Arabic and it is the most common language.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It also shares a maritime border with _____ to the northwest, away from the country's short distance.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “border”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Lebanon article.

questions.proof: It also shares a maritime border with Cyprus to the northwest, away from the country's short distance.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Lebanon has been independent since 22 November _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Lebanon article, under the heading “History & Data”.

questions.proof: Lebanon has been independent since 22 November 1943.
